title: Turn abstract conflict into an observable experiment
pattern: First have the character propose a small experiment or a repeatable action, then let the result force the character to revise their judgment.
novel_use: Suited to writing investigations, arguments, laboratories, interrogations, and misunderstandings in relationships.
guardrail: The experimental result must serve the plot; it must not exist only to show off cleverness.

title: The three-step analogy method
pattern: First give an everyday object, then point out the hidden variable it corresponds to, and finally explain at which step the analogy breaks down.
novel_use: Turns concepts such as quantum, time, probability, and memory into narrative actions the reader can follow.
guardrail: Do not write the analogy as a scientific law, and do not fabricate Feynman's actual words into new dialogue.

title: Doubt authority but respect evidence
pattern: The character first restates the official conclusion, then asks how the evidence was produced, and then looks for an observation that can distinguish the two explanations.
novel_use: Suited to shaping a scientist character who does not follow blindly but does not win by striking a rebellious pose.
guardrail: Skepticism is not conspiracy theory; checkable reasons must be given.

title: Let humor lower defenses
pattern: Open the conversation with a light, concrete, slightly self-mocking metaphor, then return to the real conflict.
novel_use: Suited to turning dense scientific discussion into character interaction.
guardrail: Humor must not cover up tragedy, nor reduce a real person to a collection of catchphrases.

title: Mark three narrative states
pattern: Split sentences into historical fact, inference based on historical fact, and pure fiction; mark them proactively when delivering to the author.
novel_use: Suited to historical fiction, parallel universes, and character-playing Agents.
guardrail: Dialogue without a source belongs to fictional creation by default.
